prompt: rgb.jpg is a horizontal strip of 5 frames, left to right in time order, sampled from the few seconds of a head-mounted (egocentric) video; the camera wearer is the viewpoint. depth.jpg, segmentation.jpg and pose.jpg are the same 5 frames rendered as a monocular depth map (brighter = nearer to the camera wearer), an instance segmentation map (coloured masks with class labels), and a body/hand skeleton map (yellow = body, magenta = hands) on black. Look at all four images. For EACH of the three maps, describe the spatial understanding that map supports, using the RGB strip for context: the layout of the scene; which people and objects are present and roughly how far each is from the camera wearer (in metres) and from each other; relative positions (left/right/in front/behind, above/below); which way people face and whether they look toward the camera wearer; what is within arm's reach of the camera wearer or of others; occlusions and anything partly out of view; and how these change across the 5 frames (approach, retreat, turning). Say what each map shows that is hard to see in the RGB alone, and where the map looks unreliable. Describe only spatial facts. Do not guess anyone's intentions, social norms, or what anyone should do. Return only JSON: {"depth": "...", "segmentation": "...", "pose": "..."} with 3-5 sentences each.

descriptions.depth: The depth map shows an indoor room where a grey furry blanket and the camera wearer's extended right arm occupy the immediate foreground at roughly 0.1 to 0.5 metres (within arm's reach), positioned in front of and below a seated man wearing glasses who starts about 1.5 to 2.0 metres away, with a potted plant to his left (~2.0 to 2.5 metres away) and walls, a keyboard stand, and glass doors behind him (~2.5 to 3.5 metres away). Across the five frames, the camera wearer lowers the blanket slightly in frame 2, lifts it in frame 3 to occlude the man's torso, brings it within 0.1 to 0.2 metres of the lens in frame 4 to completely occlude the room, and lowers it in frame 5 as the camera wearer and the man move closer together to about 0.6 to 0.8 metres (bringing the man within arm's reach as he faces forward and slightly to the right). The depth map clearly separates the foreground blanket and hand from the background room and quantifies the decreasing distance to the seated man even when motion blur and uniform grey fur texture make depth hard to judge in RGB alone. However, the map is unreliable in frame 1 where the extremely close blanket saturates the dynamic range and causes the man and background beyond ~1.5 metres to drop into nearly uniform black, and in frame 4 where the close fabric creates a flat, featureless gradient.
descriptions.segmentation: The instance segmentation map identifies the seated man in front of the camera wearer (~1.5 to 2.0 metres away initially, closing to ~0.6 to 0.8 metres in frame 5), the potted plant about 0.5 to 1.0 metre to his left and slightly behind him, and the camera wearer's own right arm and hand reaching from the bottom-right within 0.3 to 0.5 metres. It tracks how the foreground grey blanket—held in the camera wearer's hand—occludes the lower half of the man in frames 1, 3, and 5, drops mostly out of view at the bottom of frame 2, and completely blocks all background objects and people in frame 4. Compared to RGB alone, the segmentation map explicitly isolates the boundary between the camera wearer's reaching arm and the seated man's torso behind it in frames 1 and 3, where they overlap along the line of sight. However, the map is unreliable on the grey furry blanket: it misses the blanket entirely in frames 1, 2, and 4, and misclassifies it as a 'dining table' in the lower foreground of frames 3 and 5 while also failing to segment the background keyboard stand and glass doors.
descriptions.pose: The pose map tracks the upper-body skeleton and facial keypoints of the seated man in front of the camera wearer as he faces and looks toward the camera wearer in frames 1 to 3 (~1.2 to 2.0 metres away) and turns his head slightly to his left in frame 5 (~0.6 to 0.8 metres away), alongside a magenta hand skeleton for the camera wearer's right hand at ~0.3 to 0.4 metres in frame 1. In frames 1 and 2, the man's shoulders and arms are visible with his hands near his lap (within his own arm's reach), whereas in frame 3 his arms below the shoulders are occluded by the raised blanket, in frame 4 all keypoints disappear under full occlusion by the blanket, and in frame 5 only his facial keypoints and left shoulder remain in view above the blanket. The map makes the man's torso orientation, shoulder tilt, and eye/nose alignment explicit despite heavy foreground occlusion and motion blur in RGB, and pinpoints the finger articulation of the camera wearer's grasping hand in frame 1. However, the pose map is unreliable in frame 1 where it shrinks the man's torso bounding box and confuses the spatial ownership of the camera wearer's foreground hand with the man's body region, and in frame 3 where it completely misses the camera wearer's visible right hand holding the blanket.
